title: Who put this eye on your money?
parts: Who put this eye on your money?
People say a secret brotherhood did.
The paperwork tells a different story.
July fourth, seventeen seventy-six.
Congress wants a national seal.
A committee: Franklin, Jefferson, Adams.
They bring in an artist, Du Simitière.
In August, he sketches an eye inside a glowing triangle.
Du Simitière was not a Mason.
Was that eye new? No. Religious art already used it for the Trinity.
August twentieth: Congress shelves the report.
Six years. Three committees. Seventeen eighty-two.
William Barton adds an unfinished pyramid beneath the eye.
Secretary Charles Thomson combines the materials.
June twentieth, Congress approves the final design.
Where are the Masons?
On that first committee, one known Mason: Franklin.
His own ideas had no eye.
Masonic handbooks show it as standard only in the seventeen nineties.
Years after the seal.
Why does everyone link it to Masons?
Nineteen thirty-five. The dollar shows both sides of the seal.
President Roosevelt approved the bill design. He was a Mason, since nineteen eleven.
Easy to see why people link them.
But the eye was approved one hundred fifty-three years earlier.
Design story: documented.
Masons created the eye: myth.
Congress approved that eye. Look at your dollar again.
